messages:
marco: quick dump from the continuous-batcher run on stage-3 GPUs — looks worse than I expected
marco: overall pad waste reported ~34% (token-space), avg_batch_size 42 -> expected 60 under current routing
marco: KV cache overhead spiked too: +210MB per worker when sequence mix had many short + some very long seqs
marco: profiler snippet:
```
BatchProfile { avg_batch: 42, avg_seq_len: 73, pad_waste_ratio: 0.34, per_seq_overhead_kb: 1.8, kv_cache_mb: 210 }
OperatorTimes { matmul_kernel=A: 12.8ms, kernel=B: 9.3ms (but B uses 20% more workspace) }
```
sara: thanks — did you correlate pad waste to the routing policy? sounds like small-reqs are being grouped with long tails
marco: yes, routing is currently size-agnostic; two hot clients send many 8–12 token reqs which get batched with occasional 512-token requests, causing padding blowup
alex: hmm that's the classic tail-latency tradeoff — we should try: 1) size-aware bucketing, 2) prefer kernel A for low-memory runs, 3) enable workspace reuse when kernel B selected
emily: what about allocator tunables? last time we decreased min-slab to 8MB we saw fragmentation go up but peak dropped a bit
marco: allocator dump shows a lot of small live allocations from per-seq bookkeeping (seq metadata buffers) — per-seq_overhead_kb ~1.8 across most runs; if we reduce that to ~1.1 via struct packing we could save ~75MB on 42-batch avg
marco: OOM log from yesterday run attached (short):
```
[oom] gpu0: Alloc failed for size=1.1GiB while trying kernel=B
Backtrace: runtime::alloc -> kernel_launcher -> run_sequence_batch
Context: avg_batch 58 pad_waste 0.4 kv_cache 240MB
```
sara: 1. size-aware bucketing seems highest ROI; 2. kernel selection should be policy-driven: prefer kernel B when workspace budget available and kernel B win% on perf >15%
sara: can we add telemetry counters for pad_waste by bucket + kernel chosen? want per-route delta
emily: +1 on telemetry. Also think about a reclaim window after batch completes — lazy free caused by cudaStream syncs is adding temporary pressure
alex: proposal: experiment branch with three things combined: size-aware bucketing, reduced per-seq metadata (packing), and dynamic kernel preference (cost model uses workspace headroom + latency delta). measure steady-state pad_waste and OOM rate
marco: I'll wire a quick microbench: synthetic mix (70% short 8–16, 25% mid 64–128, 5% long 256–1024) and two configs: baseline vs proposed. will run on stage-3 tomorrow morning and post numbers
marco: infra-bot: create perf job for branch runtime/bucket-kernel-reclaim with config matrix (batch_target=[32,48,64], slab_min=[8MB,16MB])
infra-bot: perf job created: job_id=perf-2026-03-22-4312, queue=stage-3, ETA ~ 4h :rocket:
sara: add eval for pad_waste % and peak_mem (p95) to job metrics. if pad_waste drops >10% and peak_mem p95 drops >5% then we mark as candidate for canary
emily: also request kernel telemetry: time by kernel + workspace used; add KV hit decimals (prefetch effect)
alex: one caution — kernel B's extra workspace means more spill risk if KV cache is large; maybe autoscale kv cache target per batch based on predicted kernel choice
marco: noted. I'll include kv_cache_target toggles in job. I'll post results in this thread when done. thanks all :thumbsup:
